hero.headline: Choose the Escrow That Fits Your Deal

section1.headline: The Escrow Process
section1.description:
Choose timed escrow with Shake DeFi as arbiter, or 2-of-3 escrow with an arbiter chosen by the buyer and seller. Both hold payment in a smart contract, with different release and dispute rules. Review the selected option before signing.

2-of-3 escrow uses a separate smart contract for each deal on Base or TON. Use the asset and network offered for your transaction in the app. Wallet, token, and swap availability varies by platform and location.

cta.subhead: Create your account today and join the movement to everyday crypto.

howItWorks.escrowIntro: Choose timed escrow with Shake DeFi as arbiter, or 2-of-3 escrow with an arbiter chosen by the buyer and seller. Both hold payment in a smart contract, with different release and dispute rules. Review the selected option before signing.
howItWorks.agreementNote: For 2-of-3 escrow, buyer and seller both sign the PDF agreement before payment. Signing captures a front-camera photo; the agreement, signatures, and photos are available to the arbiter chosen by buyer and seller during a dispute. Agreement signatures are separate from later wallet authorizations to release or refund funds.
howItWorks.smartContractNote: 2-of-3 escrow uses a separate smart contract for each deal on Base or TON. Use the asset and network offered for your transaction in the app. Wallet, token, and swap availability varies by platform and location.

process.step1: After making a transaction, your money is placed into an escrow for the agreed duration (0–180 days), which is like a neutral safe, rather than going directly to the merchant.
process.step2: During the holding period, if you do not receive what you purchased, discuss it with the seller or request a refund. Shake DeFi acts as the arbiter and reviews the evidence.
process.step3: If no dispute is requested during the agreed escrow period, the merchant can withdraw funds immediately, or receive them automatically once the standard arbitration buffer concludes at the baseline fee.

options.title: Two escrow options, different rules
options.timedBody: Shake DeFi is the arbiter for timed escrow and reviews disputes. Agree on a holding period, raise disputes during that period, and release payment under its time-based rules. Standard release costs 0.1%; early withdrawal can bring the total to 1%. Zero-day payments have no escrow dispute window.
options.quorumBody: Buyer and seller choose their own arbiter for the deal. In 2-of-3 escrow, any two of the buyer, seller, and their chosen arbiter must authorize the same outcome: payment to the seller or refund to the buyer. Buyer and seller can settle together without the arbiter. Settlement is complete only after blockchain confirmation.
options.lock: 2-of-3 escrow has no automatic release date or timed dispute deadline. Funds can remain locked indefinitely without two matching authorizations. No single participant can settle alone.
options.fee: 1% deducted on release or refund: 0.5% to the arbiter and 0.5% to the protocol. Network fees may also apply.
options.identity: For 2-of-3 escrow, the arbiter chosen by buyer and seller approves both participants before agreement approval, payment, or settlement signing. Each provides their name, phone number, and address, or completes Persona ID verification. At $10,000 USD equivalent or more, Persona verification is required for both.
options.ratings: After a funded 2-of-3 deal settles, the arbiter rates both participants and each participant rates the arbiter. Buyer and seller may also rate each other under the Terms; if the arbiter authorized a refund, the seller cannot rate the buyer. Ratings never hold up release or refund.

diagram.quorumLabel: Any one of these pairs can authorize the same outcome

earning.title: Mediate transactions and earn half the settlement fee
earning.body: 2-of-3 escrow opens a new role for Shake users: serve as the arbiter chosen by the buyer and seller. Review both participants before payment and help resolve disagreements by reviewing the evidence. The chosen arbiter receives 0.5% of the transaction amount—half of the 1% settlement fee. The other 0.5% goes to the protocol.
earning.payment: The fee is paid when a funded deal settles on-chain, whether funds go to the seller or are refunded to the buyer. It also applies when buyer and seller settle together without the arbiter’s signature.

questions.question: How does the app work?
questions.answer: Choose timed escrow with Shake DeFi as arbiter, or 2-of-3 escrow with an arbiter chosen by the buyer and seller. Both hold payment in a smart contract, with different release and dispute rules. Review the selected option before signing.

questions.question: How do I get started?
questions.answer:
You can get started across multiple platforms:
- **iOS & Android**: [Download the mobile app](https://shakedefi.com) for full features, Coinbase embedded wallet, and fiat onramp/offramp.
- **Telegram**: Chat with [@ShakeDefiBot](https://t.me/ShakeDefiBot) or open the [Telegram mini-app](https://t.me/ShakeDefiBot/app) to create escrow deals and connect your Telegram wallet or Tonkeeper.
- **Farcaster**: Open the [Shake mini-app on Farcaster](https://farcaster.xyz/miniapps/4LNSH2r_Bkx7/shake-defi) and transact with your native Base ETH wallet.

questions.question: Which platforms and wallets does Shake DeFi support?
questions.answer:
Shake DeFi is available on iOS, Android, Telegram, and Farcaster, supporting:
- **Coinbase Embedded Wallet** (iOS & Android): Full feature access including fiat onramp/offramp and Rubic currency swapping.
- **Telegram Wallet & Tonkeeper** (Telegram): Transact with TON and USDT, browse the P2P Marketplace channel, or chat with [@ShakeDefiBot](https://t.me/ShakeDefiBot).
- **Native ETH Wallet** (Farcaster): Transact on the Ethereum Base network directly from your Farcaster client.

questions.question: What is Post to Marketplace?
questions.answer: Post to Marketplace is an optional way to share your Shake listing with the Shake Marketplace Telegram channel so more potential buyers can discover it.

questions.question: Do I have to share my listing with Marketplace?
questions.answer: No. Sharing is optional. You choose whether each listing is posted to the Shake Marketplace Telegram channel.

questions.question: What information appears in a Marketplace post?
questions.answer: A Marketplace post shares your listing's photo, description, price, and location so buyers can quickly understand what you are offering.

questions.question: Where can I browse Marketplace listings?
questions.answer: You can browse current listings in the [Shake Marketplace Telegram channel](https://t.me/Shake_Marketplace).

questions.question: What is Paste to Escrow?
questions.answer: Paste to Escrow lets you turn any item you find on a peer-to-peer marketplace (like Craigslist, OfferUp, or Facebook Marketplace) into a secure escrow transaction. Simply copy the listing text to your clipboard and paste it into Shake DeFi — either on the app's Payment screen or in a chat with [@ShakeDefiBot](https://t.me/ShakeDefiBot) on Telegram. Shake automatically parses the details, lets you select your desired cryptocurrency, and invites the seller to join a smart-contract-protected escrow.

questions.question: What can I do with @ShakeDefiBot on Telegram?
questions.answer: With [@ShakeDefiBot](https://t.me/ShakeDefiBot) on Telegram, you can paste any marketplace listing directly into your chat to generate an escrow contract, open the Shake Telegram mini-app, connect TON or Ethereum wallets, and pay with TON, USDT, USDC, or ETH — all without leaving Telegram.

questions.question: What is an escrow?
questions.answer: Escrow holds a payment in a smart contract while the parties complete a deal. Timed escrow uses an agreed holding period and dispute window. In 2-of-3 escrow, any two of buyer, seller, and arbiter must authorize the same release or refund; delivery alone does not release payment.

questions.question: Do I have to use an escrow period?
questions.answer: No. Timed escrow, 2-of-3 escrow, and zero-day payments without escrow are separate choices. For buyer-created invitations, the seller chooses 2-of-3 with their own arbiter, the existing 14-day holding period, or zero days without escrow. Review the choice before signing: 2-of-3 has no automatic release date.

questions.question: Do I need prior crypto experience or investment knowledge to use Shake?
questions.answer: No prior cryptocurrency experience is required. Shake makes crypto payments as straightforward as everyday payment apps. You don't have to speculate on volatile crypto markets or manage complicated seed phrases — on mobile, you can easily fund your wallet with a debit card or bank account via Coinbase Onramp and transact using price-stable assets like USDC (pegged 1:1 to the US dollar). When you receive funds, you can cash out back to your bank account with Coinbase Offramp. Shake never stores or processes fiat money directly; all escrow transactions settle securely on the blockchain.

questions.question: Who can use the Shake app?
questions.answer: Shake is for adults aged 18 and over. Identity requirements depend on the transaction. For 2-of-3 escrow, see the participant approval requirements below.

questions.question: Can I pay with any cryptocurrency I own?
questions.answer:
Yes! Shake supports flexible payment options across supported cryptocurrencies: USDC, ETH, TON, and USDT, plus Bitcoin and Staked ETH via swapping. On mobile, you can transfer cryptocurrency to your Coinbase wallet in the app and convert it using the built-in Rubic swap feature. On Telegram, you can pay with TON or USDT via your Telegram wallet or Tonkeeper. On Farcaster, you can transact directly using your native Base ETH wallet.

Note: Coinbase and Rubic swap services are not available in all countries.

questions.question: Do I have to accept any 'arbitrary' cryptocurrency as payment?
questions.answer: No, you specify which crypto you want to receive (such as USDC, ETH, TON, or USDT). When buyers pay with a different cryptocurrency like Bitcoin or Staked ETH, they use the built-in swap feature to convert it to your preferred currency before the transaction completes. You always receive exactly what you requested. When withdrawing funds, mobile users can offramp to fiat via Coinbase, while Telegram, Tonkeeper, and Farcaster users receive settled funds directly to their connected wallets.

questions.question: How long does it take to send or accept a payment? Is there an instant transfer fee?
questions.answer:
Timed escrow: Payments typically confirm on-chain in seconds. The "waiting" you see in Shake isn't transfer time—it's escrow protection. You choose an escrow duration between 0 and 180 days (for example, 3 days, or 0 for instant settlement). During this agreed window, the buyer can inspect the purchase and file a dispute if needed. After that window closes without a dispute, there is a standard 3-day arbitration buffer before automatic release at the baseline 0.1% fee. If a merchant wants to get paid immediately right when the buyer's escrow period ends, they can use early withdrawal for an additional fee (up to 0.9% additional, for a total fee of 1.0%): withdrawing earlier during the buffer incurs 0.4% (1 day early), 0.7% (2 days early), or 1.0% (3 days early). Shake does not charge a separate instant transfer fee; normal network fees may apply.

In 2-of-3 escrow, any two of the buyer, seller, and their chosen arbiter must authorize the same outcome: payment to the seller or refund to the buyer. Buyer and seller can settle together without the arbiter. Settlement is complete only after blockchain confirmation. 2-of-3 escrow has no automatic release date or timed dispute deadline. Funds can remain locked indefinitely without two matching authorizations. No single participant can settle alone.

questions.question: Are there fees to use Shake?
questions.answer: 2-of-3 escrow deducts 1% at settlement, on either payment or refund: 0.5% to the arbiter and 0.5% to the protocol. Timed escrow keeps its own fee schedule: 0.1% for standard release, with early withdrawal fees up to 1% total. Network and third-party fees may also apply.

questions.question: Do I need to report my Shake transactions on my taxes?
questions.answer:
In most countries, including the United States, cryptocurrency transactions are taxable events. This applies to Shake transactions as well. There are three main transaction types to be aware of:

1) Paying for goods or services with crypto is treated as a disposal of that asset. If the crypto's value increased since you acquired it, you may owe capital gains tax on the difference.
2) Swapping between cryptocurrencies (e.g., converting Bitcoin to USDC via Shake's built-in swap feature) is also generally treated as a taxable event in the U.S.
3) Receiving crypto as a merchant is typically treated as ordinary income at the fair market value at the time of receipt.

Crypto tax tools like [CoinLedger](https://coinledger.io) and [Koinly](https://koinly.io) make this process straightforward. They can import your on-chain transaction history — including Shake transactions, which are permanently recorded on the blockchain — and automatically calculate your gains, losses, and income.

questions.question: Are there any income requirements to use Shake?
questions.answer: No, there are no income requirements to use Shake.

questions.question: Can I accept international transactions with Shake?
questions.answer: Yes, you can accept international transactions from any other Shake user.

questions.question: In which countries is Shake not available?
questions.answer: Shake is not available in Brazil, Mexico, Taiwan, Japan, and United Kingdom.

questions.question: Are there any spending requirements, limits or transaction caps?
questions.answer: There are no spending limits or transaction caps imposed by Shake itself.

questions.question: What happens if there is a dispute?
questions.answer: With timed escrow, Shake DeFi is the arbiter. The buyer must open a dispute within the agreed holding period, and Shake DeFi reviews the evidence under the timed escrow rules. With 2-of-3 escrow, buyer and seller choose their own arbiter, who reviews evidence and can authorize an outcome together with either participant. The chosen arbiter cannot move funds alone.

questions.question: How does Shake protect against fraud and unauthorized transactions?
questions.answer: Shake protects against fraud and unauthorized transactions with verified identities, signed agreements for each transaction, and verifiable on-chain proof of payment, backed by detailed records for dispute resolution.

questions.question: Who can authorize escrow settlement?
questions.answer: In 2-of-3 escrow, any two of the buyer, seller, and their chosen arbiter must authorize the same outcome: payment to the seller or refund to the buyer. Buyer and seller can settle together without the arbiter. Settlement is complete only after blockchain confirmation.

questions.question: What is documented when I make a transaction?
questions.answer: For 2-of-3 escrow, buyer and seller both sign the PDF agreement before payment. Signing captures a front-camera photo; the agreement, signatures, and photos are available to the arbiter chosen by buyer and seller during a dispute. Agreement signatures are separate from later wallet authorizations to release or refund funds.

questions.question: How does Shake create accountability?
questions.answer: For 2-of-3 escrow, the arbiter chosen by buyer and seller approves both participants before agreement approval, payment, or settlement signing. Each provides their name, phone number, and address, or completes Persona ID verification. At $10,000 USD equivalent or more, Persona verification is required for both.

questions.question: What information is public?
questions.answer: While transactions are recorded on the blockchain (which is publicly viewable but anonymous), personal Shake accounts and blockchain accounts are not publicly associated.

questions.question: Is there support for splitting shared expenses amongst a group?
questions.answer: While this isn't currently supported, it is on our roadmap for future implementation.

questions.question: Where is Shake Defi incorporated?
questions.answer: Shake Defi, Inc. is incorporated in Brookfield, Wisconsin, United States .

questions.question: Can I earn money as an arbiter?
questions.answer:
2-of-3 escrow opens a new role for Shake users: serve as the arbiter chosen by the buyer and seller. Review both participants before payment and help resolve disagreements by reviewing the evidence. The chosen arbiter receives 0.5% of the transaction amount—half of the 1% settlement fee. The other 0.5% goes to the protocol.

The fee is paid when a funded deal settles on-chain, whether funds go to the seller or are refunded to the buyer. It also applies when buyer and seller settle together without the arbiter’s signature.

steps.description: With timed escrow, Shake DeFi is the arbiter. The buyer must open a dispute within the agreed holding period, and Shake DeFi reviews the evidence under the timed escrow rules. With 2-of-3 escrow, buyer and seller choose their own arbiter, who reviews evidence and can authorize an outcome together with either participant. The chosen arbiter cannot move funds alone.

nonCustodial.title: Non-Custodial by Design
nonCustodial.lead: Shake does not take custody of escrowed customer funds.
nonCustodial.body1: 2-of-3 escrow uses a separate smart contract for each deal on Base or TON. Use the asset and network offered for your transaction in the app. Wallet, token, and swap availability varies by platform and location.
nonCustodial.body2: You use your connected wallet to authorize transactions.

cryptocurrency.headline: Use the Cryptocurrency You Already Have
cryptocurrency.body1: Shake supports USDC and USDT, along with ETH, TON, and other supported cryptocurrencies.
cryptocurrency.body2: The seller can specify the cryptocurrency they want to receive. Where supported, buyers can use integrated currency-swapping functionality to convert another supported cryptocurrency into the required payment currency.
cryptocurrency.body3: Shake is designed around cryptocurrency payments, but you do not need investment expertise to understand the basic transaction process: agree on terms, fund the escrow, complete the transaction, and release the payment according to those terms.

fiatConversion.headline: Optional Fiat Conversion
fiatConversion.body1: On supported mobile platforms and in eligible locations, Coinbase provides optional fiat onramp and offramp services.
fiatConversion.body2: You can use Coinbase to purchase supported cryptocurrency using available payment methods or convert cryptocurrency back to fiat.
fiatConversion.disclaimer: Shake does not hold your fiat money or operate the Coinbase conversion service. Coinbase availability, supported assets, payment methods, and fees vary by country.

fees.headline: Transparent Fees
fees.body1: 2-of-3 escrow deducts 1% at settlement, on either payment or refund: 0.5% to the arbiter and 0.5% to the protocol. Timed escrow keeps its own fee schedule: 0.1% for standard release, with early withdrawal fees up to 1% total. Network and third-party fees may also apply.
fees.body2: 2-of-3 escrow has no automatic release date or timed dispute deadline. Funds can remain locked indefinitely without two matching authorizations. No single participant can settle alone.
fees.body3: Blockchain network fees may also apply. Third-party services such as cryptocurrency conversion and swapping may have their own fees.
fees.noSubscriptions: ✓ There are no recurring subscription fees for basic Shake use.

identityRecords.headline: Identity and Transaction Records
identityRecords.lead: For 2-of-3 escrow, the arbiter chosen by buyer and seller approves both participants before agreement approval, payment, or settlement signing. Each provides their name, phone number, and address, or completes Persona ID verification. At $10,000 USD equivalent or more, Persona verification is required for both.
identityRecords.body1: For 2-of-3 escrow, buyer and seller both sign the PDF agreement before payment. Signing captures a front-camera photo; the agreement, signatures, and photos are available to the arbiter chosen by buyer and seller during a dispute. Agreement signatures are separate from later wallet authorizations to release or refund funds.
identityRecords.body2: With timed escrow, Shake DeFi is the arbiter. The buyer must open a dispute within the agreed holding period, and Shake DeFi reviews the evidence under the timed escrow rules. With 2-of-3 escrow, buyer and seller choose their own arbiter, who reviews evidence and can authorize an outcome together with either participant. The chosen arbiter cannot move funds alone.

disclaimerBanner.body2: Cryptocurrency is used as the payment method for transactions.
